quotes.text: The cloud hides the machinery, but not the logic. Shared pools, contention and scheduling didn't vanish, They've just become transparent to the end user.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why mainframe-era resource thinking still matters in Azure.

quotes.text: Running computing power as a shared pool has always been cheaper and more adaptable than everyone buying and maintaining their own hardware.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the economic reason centralized computing keeps returning.

quotes.text: Graphical interfaces win for discoverability, while terminals win for precision and repeatability. That trade off is exactly why the terminal quietly staged its return.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear rule of thumb for choosing between GUI and command line.

quotes.text: Machines, whether Altair or Azure, can only follow the instructions you give them. AI generated code or a workflow template often falls apart when the underlying intent isn't clear.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links clear intent and systems thinking to success with modern tools.

quotes.text: When you call an API for an automated workflow plan for logging and error handling. Just as carefully as you plan the logic, capture enough structured information that you can map outcomes back to original intent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical observability recommendation for API-based automation.

People and the hidden soft skills

takeaways: Constraints create clarity: the Altair 8800 forced precise, efficient design, and the same habit pays off when sizing cloud resources and building flows.
Centralization returns for efficiency, so Azure and Microsoft 365 work like a globally scaled mainframe with shared pools, contention and scheduling hidden underneath.
Systems thinking still wins: terminals, scripts and APIs reward clear intent, documentation and observability more than any single tool.
hook: Cloud platforms look nothing like a 1975 box of switches, yet Azure still runs on the same ideas of shared resources and programmable access. This episode is for IT pros, developers and Power Platform makers who want to reason more clearly about cloud architecture and cost. You learn how mainframe and terminal patterns explain modern design choices and how to apply them to automation today.
